equity_bridge.note: 10-Q 2026-06-30 balance sheet, noncontrolling interests at book

equity_bridge.item: Q4 FY26 cash generation to FY-end, net of Q4 dividend
equity_bridge.note: FY26 OCF guidance 'at least $3.0B' (reiterated 2026-07-21) less 9M actual $880.8M = >= $2,119M Q4 OCF; less ~$40M Q4 capex and ~$127M Aug-26 dividend; rounded down. Q4 buybacks (~$0.3B) not deducted because the share count is held at the June count.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: equity_3yr_cagr (FY22-FY25); the 5yr equity and EPS CAGRs start from the FY2020 pre-boom base and embed the 2021-22 margin peak
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 15.3% vs revenue 5yr 11.0% (39% divergence) and equity 3yr 7.7% vs revenue 3yr 0.8% / EPS 3yr -11.3%: retained earnings from peak-margin years compounded book faster than the business grew. Cyclical distortion, not a durable compounding rate.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF = reported FCF - SBC - equity-award withholding taxes (interest income 0, net debt). FCF CAGRs are meaningless for a homebuilder: FY2022 owner FCF was only $246.5M because $5.2B went into inventory at the top of the cycle, while FY2023 released it ($4.2B). Owner-FCF 5yr CAGR (20.6%) is slightly below reported (19.9% -> small gap) -- SBC is ~0.6% of revenue and not a material driver. Growth anchors for the projection are the revenue history (10yr 12.2% incl. share gains and the boom; 3yr 0.8%) and the FY26 guidance (-4.4%).

scenario_narratives.base: Affordability-constrained FY27 with elevated incentives, then mid-single-digit volume growth on the structural single-family shortage and share gains; margins recover to mid-cycle (~14% pre-tax), not to the FY21-24 peak.
scenario_narratives.bull: Mortgage rates fall toward 5.5%, incentives unwind, gross margin rebuilds to ~24-25% and pre-tax margin settles ~16%; volume reaches 95-100k closings by FY30.
scenario_narratives.bear: Affordability squeeze becomes a housing downturn: revenue -10% over two years, pre-tax margin troughs ~10% with impairments, and mid-cycle margin resets ~1.5pp lower; inventory liquidation cushions cash flow.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Mid-cycle owner-FCF DCF for a cyclical homebuilder. The value driver is not margin extrapolation but (i) where the pre-tax margin settles through the cycle and (ii) how much inventory each dollar of growth consumes. Peak FY21-24 margins are excluded from the base; working capital is modelled on the change in revenue so growth costs cash and downturns release it. Terminal value capped at 12x owner FCF.
key_risks_to_valuation: Mortgage rates: the incentive (rate-buydown) spend that compressed gross margin from ~27% (FY22) to 20.7% (Q3 FY26) is rate-driven and outside management's control.
Mid-cycle margin judgment: each 1pp of terminal EBITDA margin is worth roughly $10-12/share.
Working-capital intensity: if land-light optioning stalls, growth consumes more inventory than the -70% capture assumes.
Housing downturn with land impairments (FY2008-2011 precedent) would push through the bear case.
Forestar dependence for lot supply and the NCI/related-party structure.
Policy: 45L credit expiry, tariffs on materials, immigration effects on construction labour.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 131.75-176.22.
data_sources.financials: research/DHI/Reports/DHI_Metrics.csv (SEC XBRL, annual rows FY2008-FY2025); SEC companyfacts API for pre-tax income, interest in cost of sales, D&A, NCI, diluted shares; 10-Q for quarter ended 2026-06-30 (filed 2026-07-23) for notes payable by segment, mortgage loans held for sale, share count.
data_sources.qualitative: Q3 FY2026 earnings release (8-K Ex. 99.1, 2026-07-21): FY26 revenue guidance $32.5-33.0B, 83.8-84.3k closings, ~25% tax rate, OCF >= $3.0B, ~$2.5B buybacks, ~$500M dividends; Q3 home sales gross margin 20.7%, cancellation rate 20%. 10-Q MD&A: incentives expected to remain elevated into fiscal 2027. No Analysis.json existed at build time.

inputs.base_revenue_note: FY2026E = midpoint of the updated FY26 consolidated revenue guidance ($32.5-33.0B, Q3 FY26 release 2026-07-21). FY26 ends 2026-09-30, four days after the valuation date, so FY2026 is treated as FY0 and Y1 = FY2027. 9M FY26 actual revenue $23,672.2M.
inputs.share_count_basis: 280.73M shares outstanding at 2026-06-30 (10-Q cover/balance sheet) plus ~0.8M dilutive RSUs (Q3 FY26 weighted diluted 283.0M less weighted basic 282.2M). Held FLAT: SBC incl. equity-award withholding taxes is expensed in the flows; DHI is a heavy repurchaser ($4.3B FY25, $2.2B 9M FY26, ~$2.5B FY26 guidance) so the flat count is funded, and repurchases beyond SBC offset are treated as a use of the owner FCF already valued, not as extra value.
inputs.debt_note: Notes payable at 2026-06-30 (10-Q Note F): homebuilding $3,685.3M + rental $820.3M + Forestar $793.8M = $5,299.4M. EXCLUDED: financial-services mortgage repurchase facilities $1,813.2M, which are operating funding secured on $2,990.6M of mortgage loans held for sale (treated like deposits at a lender: the mortgage book is working capital of the financial-services segment whose pre-tax income is in the flows). Cash $2,078.7M consolidated (includes Forestar). All homebuilding interest is capitalised to inventory and expensed through cost of sales, so EBITDA below is built pre-interest (interest in COGS added back) to keep the flows unlevered against a net-debt bridge.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash-flow statement: stock-based compensation $131.0M add-back + $64.2M taxes paid on net-share settlement of equity awards (financing activities); DHI publishes no combined adjusted-EBITDA SBC figure, so the two lines are summed. 9M FY26: $107.5M SBC + $55.2M withholding.
inputs.interest_income_note: 0: DHI carries net debt; interest earned on cash sits in 'other income' and is immaterial.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 repurchases $4.3B (PaymentsForRepurchaseOfCommonStock); 9M FY26 $2.2B; FY26 guidance ~$2.5B; $1.1B authorization remaining at 2026-06-30.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate. Risk-free ~4.3% (10y UST), ERP 5.0%, levered beta ~1.35 for US homebuilders -> cost of equity ~11.0%; debt ~12% of market capital at ~5% pre-tax (3.8% after tax) -> WACC ~10.1%, set at 10.0%. Same WACC in all three scenarios: housing-cycle risk is charged in the scenario flows and weights, not a stacked premium (adaptations 7f).
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP (ASC 842): operating lease cost already sits in SG&A/cost of sales, so EBITDA is post-lease; lease liabilities (accrued expenses) are excluded from net debt. One treatment, not two.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are 100%-consolidated (Forestar ~62% owned, consolidated). NCI charged once in the equity bridge at its 2026-06-30 book value of $587.0M; no NCI leakage in the flows.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF with cyclical adaptations (dcf-methods routing row 'operating company, cyclical'). D.R. Horton is an operating homebuilder that generates positive through-cycle cash flow, not a land subdivider with structurally negative FCF, so the blended NTA P/B + P/E row does not apply; its lot-option (asset-light) model puts 67% of closings on Forestar/third-party lots. Mid-cycle normalisation: the FY2021-FY2024 pre-tax margins (17-23%) were a pandemic/low-rate peak and are NOT extrapolated; the path starts from the FY26 trough-ish ~12.4% pre-tax margin (elevated mortgage-rate buydowns, guided to persist into FY27) and recovers only to a ~14% pre-tax mid-cycle level, close to the FY2015-FY2025 average ex-boom. EBITDA here = pre-tax income + interest amortised in cost of sales + D&A + SBC (FY25: 4,740 + 158 + 101 + 131 = 5,130 = 15.0% of revenue; FY26E ~13.7%). WORKING CAPITAL is the dominant cash driver for a homebuilder: inventory grew $14.0B for $16.7B of revenue growth FY19-FY25 (0.84x), so wc_capture is -70% on the change in revenue (lower than history because of the rising share of optioned lots) -- growth consumes cash and a downturn releases it, as FY2023's $4.3B OCF showed. FY0 is FY2026E; the Q4 FY26 cash generation between the 2026-06-30 balance sheet and FY-end is carried in the equity bridge (see equity_bridge). DATA NOTE: the Metrics.csv quarterly labels on the income-statement/balance-sheet rows are shifted one quarter early for FY2021-FY2026 (e.g. CSV 'Q2 2026' revenue 9,227.1 and equity 24,406.5 are the quarter ended 2026-06-30, i.e. Q3 FY26); annual rows are correct and are the only rows this model uses. TotalDebt is blank in the CSV; debt taken from the 10-Q note.

bear.narrative: A labour-market softening turns the affordability squeeze into a housing downturn: orders fall, cancellations (already 20% in Q3 FY26 vs 17%) rise, and DHI defends pace with deeper buydowns and price cuts, plus land impairments. Revenue falls ~10% over FY27-28 and pre-tax margin troughs ~10%. Recovery is slow and mid-cycle margin resets ~1.5pp lower as resale supply normalises and incentives become structural. Inventory liquidation releases cash in the downturn, cushioning the value.

base.growth_rates_rationale: FY27 +1%: orders flat YoY in Q3 FY26 and incentives guided elevated into FY27. FY28-FY30 4-6%: US single-family undersupply plus DHI share gains at the affordable entry level, a normalisation of volume without a price boom. Fades to 3% nominal (household formation ~1% + house-price inflation ~2%) by FY36.
base.ebitda_margin_rationale: Pre-SBC, pre-interest-in-COGS EBITDA. FY26E ~13.7% (9M pre-tax 12.2%, gross margin 20.7% in Q3 on rate buydowns). Recovers to 15.3% (~14% pre-tax) by FY30 -- the mid-cycle level, below FY25's 15.0% only marginally and far below the FY22 peak of ~23.8%.
base.sbc_pct_rationale: SBC 0.38-0.45% of revenue plus equity-award withholding ~0.19% = ~0.6%, held flat (no guidance of decline).
base.capex_rationale: PP&E capex only (FY25 $137M = 0.40%; 9M FY26 0.45%). Land, lots, homes under construction and rental properties are inventory and run through wc_capture.
base.cash_tax_rationale: FY26 guided income-tax rate ~25.0% (up from 23.6% FY25 as the 45L energy-efficient-home credit winds down); cash taxes paid tracked the provision (FY25 $1,020.5M paid vs $1,119M expense).
base.terminal_rationale: Cyclical cap 12x terminal owner FCF (method range 12-15x for cyclicals); Gordon at 10%/3% is ~14.7x, so the cap binds. 12x FCF is ~12x mid-cycle earnings less growth inventory, in line with where DHI has traded through the cycle.
base.narrative: Housing stays affordability-constrained through FY27 with incentives elevated, then mortgage rates drift lower and the structural US single-family shortage supports mid-single-digit volume growth. DHI's entry-level product, lot-option model (Forestar + third-party lots) and scale keep it gaining share; margins recover to mid-cycle, not peak.

bull.narrative: Mortgage rates fall toward 5.5% by FY28, unlocking pent-up first-time-buyer demand while resale inventory stays locked in by low-coupon owners. Incentives unwind, gross margin returns to ~24-25% and pre-tax margin settles ~16% (between mid-cycle and the FY23-24 level). DHI closes 95-100k homes by FY30; build-to-rent and Forestar add volume.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 12x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 25% (up from the 15% default): demand is visibly softening (cancellations 20% vs 17%, orders flat, incentives guided elevated into FY27) and homebuilders are among the most cyclical operating businesses in the folder. Base 50%: the mid-cycle recovery path. Bull 25% (down from 35%): it needs both a material fall in mortgage rates and incentive unwind, two things outside management's control. Balance sheet risk is low (debt/cap 23%), so the bear is a margin-and-volume case, not a solvency case.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
